patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH] media: redrat3: fix UAF in probe error path leaving rc device registered

version_history.subject: [PATCH] media: redrat3: fix UAF in probe error path leaving rc device registered

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch fixes a use-after-free (UAF) bug in the redrat3 driver's probe error path, where the rc device is left registered after its associated structure rr3 is freed. The fix involves unregistering and freeing the rc device before freeing rr3, matching the order used in the driver's disconnect function.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH] wifi: mac80211: avoid WARN in set_bitrate_mask when sdata not in driver

version_history.subject: [PATCH] wifi: mac80211: avoid WARN in set_bitrate_mask when sdata not in driver

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the mac80211 wireless driver where a WARN message is triggered when setting the bitrate mask for an interface that is not currently managed by the driver. The patch adds a check to ensure that the interface is still present in the driver before attempting to set the bitrate mask, returning -ENETDOWN if it is not. This change is safe because the wiphy mutex is held during the relevant operations and the IN_DRIVER flag is set/cleared under RTNL and wiphy paths.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH] fbdev: bitblit: bound-check glyph index in bit_cursor()

version_history.subject: [PATCH] fbdev: bitblit: bound-check glyph index in bit_cursor()

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch fixes a global out-of-bounds access in the bit_cursor() function of the fbdev driver by adding bounds checking to prevent an index exceeding the font's glyph count.

review_comments.author: Helge Deller
review_comments.summary: Identified a global out-of-bounds access in bit_cursor() and suggested applying bounds checking to prevent it. Patch applied successfully.
review_comments.raw_body:
On 8/8/26 04:19, Rik van Riel wrote:
> bit_cursor() fetches the glyph under the cursor with
> 
> 	c = scr_readw(vc_pos);
> 	src = vc_font.data + ((c & charmask) * w * height);
> 
> where charmask is 0x1ff when vc_hi_font_mask is set. The screen buffer
> value comes directly from scr_readw() and may be larger than the current
> font's glyph count.
> 
> Syzkaller triggers this via vcs_write(). The Call Trace shows
> vcs_write() in vc_screen.c writing an arbitrary 16-bit value with
> writev() to /dev/vcsa, which vcs_write_buf() in vc_screen.c stores via
> vcs_scr_writew() without checking charcount. The stored value is later
> read in bit_cursor() in bitblit.c.
> 
> When the font is changed from a font with 512 glyphs to a font with
> 256 glyphs, the screen buffer can retain characters with the high
> bit set from the previous mode, which could also produce the same
> out-of-bounds access.
> 
>    BUG: KASAN: global-out-of-bounds in soft_cursor+0x378/0x6bc drivers/video/fbdev/core/softcursor.c:70
>    Read of size 16 at addr ffff800086c57970
> 
>    Call Trace:
>     soft_cursor+0x378/0x6bc drivers/video/fbdev/core/softcursor.c:70
>     bit_cursor+0xa90/0x1108 drivers/video/fbdev/core/bitblit.c:365
>     fbcon_cursor+0x344/0x498 drivers/video/fbdev/core/fbcon.c:1427
>     hide_cursor+0xdc/0x2d0 drivers/tty/vt/vt.c:883
>     update_region+0x100/0x18c drivers/tty/vt/vt.c:669
>     vcs_write+0x8ec/0xaf0 drivers/tty/vt/vc_screen.c:685
> 
> bit_putcs_aligned() and bit_putcs_unaligned() already clamp the glyph
> index to vc_font.charcount. Apply the same clamp in bit_cursor() after
> extracting the attribute and masking, before indexing fontdata.
> 
> The fix completes the bounds checking started in commit 18c4ef4e765a
> ("fbdev: bitblit: bound-check glyph index in bit_putcs*"), which missed
> the cursor path.
> 
> This change should be safe because the clamp reuses the existing
> contract from fbcon: charcount is maintained under console_lock in
> con_font_set() and fbcon_font_set(), and hi_font_mask is cleared when
> switching from 512 to 256 glyphs. When stale screen data with high bits
> remains after a font switch, or when vcs_write() stores an arbitrary
> value, clamping the index to 0 prevents the out-of-bounds read without
> changing cursor semantics — the same fallback bit_putcs uses.
> 
> Reported-by: syzbot+61b1db46218109869c14@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
> Closes: https://syzkaller.appspot.com/bug?extid=61b1db46218109869c14
> Link: https://lore.kernel.org/all/6a75205c.01d0871a.3a0d52.0032.GAE@google.com/
> Fixes: 18c4ef4e765a ("fbdev: bitblit: bound-check glyph index in bit_putcs*")
> Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
> Assisted-by: Hermes:muse-spark-1.2 syzkaller
> Signed-off-by: Rik van Riel <riel@surriel.com>
> ---
>   drivers/video/fbdev/core/bitblit.c | 9 +++++++--
>   1 file changed, 7 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)
Patch applied to fbdev git tree.
Thanks!
Helge

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v3] memcg: keep folio's objcg same as its node

version_history.subject: [PATCH] memcg: keep folio's objcg same as its node
[PATCH v2] memcg: keep folio's objcg same as its node
[PATCH v3] memcg: keep folio's objcg same as its node

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch fixes a problem in the Linux kernel's memory cgroup (memcg) implementation where folio migration across nodes breaks the assumption that a folio's objcg is the same as its node. The patch ensures that the objcg of a folio is always updated to match its new node when it is migrated, and also updates the LRU list reparenting logic to be atomic with the objcg reparenting. This fixes a race condition between migration and reparenting where an LRU operation on a folio could take the wrong lock. The patch makes changes to several functions in mm/memcontrol.c to implement this fix.
